March 2026

Office for Students (OfS): non-executive board members

The Secretary of State for Education has appointed Evelyn Asante-Mensah, Kirstin Baker, Sumita Hutchison, Julia Mundy and Richard Stables to the board of the Office for Students (OfS) as non-executive board members.

Evelyn, Kirstin, Sumita, Julia and Richard have been appointed for 5 years from 1 May 2026.

Remuneration for this role is £9,180 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 20 days per year.

This appointment has been made under Schedule 1, paragraph 2(1)(d) of the Higher Education and Research Act 2017, which permits the appointment of up to 12 ordinary or non-executive OfS board members.

The register of interests of board members is published on the Office for Students website.

Evelyn has declared the following interests:

Chair, The Union (Manchester Metropolitan University Students’ Union)

Kirstin has declared the following interests:

Inquiry Chair, Competition and Markets Authority

Interim Chair, The Pensions Regulator

Co-Chair, Brighton, Hove & Sussex Sixth Form College

Julia has declared the following interests:

Academic Staff, University of Greenwich

Finance Trustee, Royal Museums Greenwich

Lay Council Member, Nursing & Midwifery Council

Independent Member, Audit and Risk Assurance Committee, UK Statistics Authority

Richard has declared the following interests:

Governor at St Chad’s College, an independent recognised College of Durham University

Sumita has declared the following interests:

Governor, Bristol Grammar School

Evelyn Asante-Mensah, Kirstin Baker, Sumita Hutchison, Julia Mundy and Richard Stables have not declared any political activity.

The OfS is a non-departmental public body and the independent regulator of higher education in England.

Student Loans Company: non-executive board member

Natasha Toothill has been reappointed to serve a second term on the Student Loans Company (SLC) board. She will serve from 1 April 2026 for a period of 3 years.

Remuneration is £12,000 a year, rising to a maximum of £17,000 a year depending on participation in board sub-committees or other additional duties as agreed with the SLC Chair. The appointment will involve an estimated time commitment of 1.5 to 2 days a month.

Natasha Toothill has not declared any conflicts of interest or political activities.

The SLC is a non-profit making government-owned organisation that administers loans and grants to students in colleges and universities in the UK. It is a non-departmental public body of the Department for Education.

February 2026

Student Loans Company: Chair

The Secretary of State for Education and ministers in the Devolved Administrations have appointed Gary Page to serve as Chair of the Student Loans Company (SLC) board. He will serve from 1 April 2026 for a period of 3 years.

Remuneration is £59,000 a year for an estimated time commitment of 8 days per month.

Gary has not declared any conflicts of interest or political activities.

SLC is a non-departmental public body of the Department for Education. Chair appointments for the SLC are made by the Secretary of State for Education and agreed by ministers in the devolved administrations.

Office for Students (OfS): non-executive board member

Caleb Stevens has been reappointed as a non-executive board member for the Office for Students (OfS) from 1 February 2026 for a period of 2 years.

Remuneration is £9,180 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 20 days, which will be pro-rated.

Caleb has declared the following interests:

Postgraduate student at the University of Exeter

Employed as the Parliamentary Safeguarding Lead for UK Parliament

Presiding Justice for the Judiciary (Cornwall District Bench)

Director of Safeguarding Central Ltd

He has not declared any political activity.

The OfS is an arm’s-length body of the Department for Education and the regulator of higher education in England.

January 2026

Ofsted: board members

Hardip Begol, Jo Coburn, Lucy Heller, Frances Wadsworth and Sir Alan Wood have been appointed to serve on the board of the Office for Standards in Education, Children’s Services and Skills (Ofsted).

Jo Coburn, Lucy Heller, Frances Wadsworth and Sir Alan Wood will serve for a period of 3 years from 1 February 2026. Hardip Begol will serve for a period of 3 years from 1 August 2026.

Remuneration is £8,292 per annum for a time commitment of 20 days per year.

Reappointed board member

David Meyer has been reappointed to serve as a board member at Ofsted. He will serve for another period of 3 years from 1 February 2026.

Office for Students: non-executive board member

Martin Coleman’s appointment as board member for the Office for Students is extended for 3 months from 1st July 2025.

Remuneration is £9,180 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 20 days, pro rata.

Read the OfS board members’ register of interest.

Martin has not declared any political activity.

June 2025

Department for Education: non-executive board members

Stuart McMinnies and Peter Bazalgette are reappointed as non-executive board members for the Department for Education from 1 June 2025 for a period of 3 years.

Remuneration is £15,000 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 24 days per year.

Read the Department for Education board members’ register of interest: March 2024.

Stuart McMinnies and Sir Peter Bazalgette have not declared any political activity.

The Department for Education’s departmental board comprises the Secretary of State, executive officials and non-executive board members.

Office for Students: interim chair

David Behan’s appointment is extended by exception as interim Chair of the Office for Students board from 25 May to 6 July 2025.

Remuneration is £29,500 per annum on the basis that Sir David will devote one day a week to this role.

David has not declared any interests or any political activity.

The OfS is an arms-length body of the Department for Education and the regulator of higher education in England.

Social Work England: non-executive directors

Cheryl Hobson, Amrat Khorana and Chris Nicholson will serve on the Social Work England board from 16 June 2025 for a period of 4 years. Cheryl is appointed as the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee Chair.

Remuneration is £350 per day for an estimated time commitment of 25 days a year, with an additional 5 days for the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee Chair role.
